fr:title.text: Freely transported terms in dependent type theory

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: Freely transported terms in dependent type theory

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Given A and B : A \to \mathbf {Type} we can make sense of transported terms along equalities between indices in A. Say, with \mathsf {subst} : {\mathopen {}\left (p : a = a'\right )\mathclose {}} \to B\,a \to B\,a' for a,a' : A.
For instance, if p : a = a' and b : B\,a then \mathsf {subst}\,p\,b : B\,a'

To avoid landing in transport hell, I suspect that it may be preferable to work inside of a description of freely transported terms instead of taking semantic transports. The hypothesis is that by using descriptions of formal transport rather than actually computing a transport, we may defer the computation of an actual transport until the end of a construction. So instead of working with B\,a directly, perhaps we may work with
\mathsf {FreeSubst}\,B\,a \colonequals \mathchoice {\textstyle \sum _{{\mathopen {}\left (a' : A\right )\mathclose {}}}}{\textstyle \sum _{{\mathopen {}\left (a' : A\right )\mathclose {}}}}{\scriptstyle \sum _{{\mathopen {}\left (a' : A\right )\mathclose {}}}}{\scriptscriptstyle \sum _{{\mathopen {}\left (a' : A\right )\mathclose {}}}} \mathchoice {\textstyle \sum _{{\mathopen {}\left (p : a = a'\right )\mathclose {}}}}{\textstyle \sum _{{\mathopen {}\left (p : a = a'\right )\mathclose {}}}}{\scriptstyle \sum _{{\mathopen {}\left (p : a = a'\right )\mathclose {}}}}{\scriptscriptstyle \sum _{{\mathopen {}\left (p : a = a'\right )\mathclose {}}}} B\,a'

I think that this is very closely related to the Fording trick, as a map out of \mathsf {FreeSubst}\,B\,a,
f : \mathchoice {\textstyle \sum _{{\mathopen {}\left (a' : A\right )\mathclose {}}}}{\textstyle \sum _{{\mathopen {}\left (a' : A\right )\mathclose {}}}}{\scriptstyle \sum _{{\mathopen {}\left (a' : A\right )\mathclose {}}}}{\scriptscriptstyle \sum _{{\mathopen {}\left (a' : A\right )\mathclose {}}}} \mathchoice {\textstyle \sum _{{\mathopen {}\left (p : a = a'\right )\mathclose {}}}}{\textstyle \sum _{{\mathopen {}\left (p : a = a'\right )\mathclose {}}}}{\scriptstyle \sum _{{\mathopen {}\left (p : a = a'\right )\mathclose {}}}}{\scriptscriptstyle \sum _{{\mathopen {}\left (p : a = a'\right )\mathclose {}}}} B\,a' \to C
can instead be described as a map,
g : {\mathopen {}\left (a' : A\right )\mathclose {}} \to {\mathopen {}\left (p : a = a'\right )\mathclose {}} \to B\,a' \to C
